root_cause.text: An incorrect boundary check in `hvc_iucv_get_private()` uses a strict greater-than comparison (`>`) instead of a greater-than-or-equal comparison (`>=`) against `hvc_iucv_devices`, allowing an out-of-bounds access to `hvc_iucv_table` when the requested index equals the maximum number of devices.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the condition in `hvc_iucv_get_private()` being corrected from `if (num > hvc_iucv_devices)` to `if (num >= hvc_iucv_devices)` before returning `hvc_iucv_table[num]`. The CVE description explains that when `hvc_iucv_devices` is 8, the original check allows accessing `hvc_iucv_table[8]`, which exceeds the 8-element limit of `hvc_iucv_table`.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function `hvc_iucv_get_private()` contains the vulnerable boundary check: `if (num > hvc_iucv_devices)`. Since the valid indices for `hvc_iucv_table` are from `0` to `hvc_iucv_devices - 1`, a value of `num` equal to `hvc_iucv_devices` will bypass this check and result in an out-of-bounds access at `hvc_iucv_table[num]`. The check should use `>=` instead of `>`.
